# Leeks Terminal (https://www.win9you.com/)

> **What this is.** A rule-based trading decision-support site. Every signal is
> computed deterministically in Python from daily OHLC bars. An LLM writes the
> explanatory text on some pages; it does not produce any number, level or verdict.
> Signals always use the previous session's close (T-1), never live intraday data.
> Educational use only — not investment advice.

Data as of the T-1 session. v2 engine coverage: 235 US and
201 Japanese stocks. Hong Kong (241 stocks) is served by
the older v1 engine and is NOT covered by v2 — read /hk200/ as a legacy signal set,
not a v2 one.

## Key pages
- [Home](https://www.win9you.com/): today's action plan and market regime summary
- [HK signals](https://www.win9you.com/hk200/) · [US signals](https://www.win9you.com/us200/) · [JP signals](https://www.win9you.com/jp200/): one table per market
- [Methodology](https://www.win9you.com/methodology): the current rule set, the measured results, and a correction log of what was changed and why
- [Backtest](https://www.win9you.com/backtest): swing vs day-trade performance, with cost assumptions stated
- [About](https://www.win9you.com/about/): who runs this and how it is funded
- [Disclaimer](https://www.win9you.com/disclaimer)

## The current rule set (v2)
1. **Long only.**
2. **Stock filter** — T-1 close above its own 200-day moving average, and that
   200-day average rising over the previous 20 sessions.
3. **Market filter** — the market index's T-1 close above its own 200-day average.
4. **Guard rails** — ATR% below 6%, 20-day box width below 35%.
5. **Entry** — limit buy at S1 (the 20-day low through T-1). The session must open
   above S1, trade down to it, **and close at or above S1**. A touch that closes
   below S1 is treated as a failed level and is not filled. This close-hold rule
   was added on 2026-10-05 after an A/B test showed it roughly doubled the
   per-trade result in all four windows.
6. **Stop** — S1 x (1 - 3 x ATR%), fixed at entry and never widened.
7. **Exit** — no price target; time exit at the close of the 10th session after entry.
8. **Sizing** — 1% of equity risked per trade, 10% notional per name, max 10
   concurrent positions. Share counts are floored to whole trading units
   (100 shares for Japan); a name that cannot be sized within those limits at
   the stated capital is published as "no order today", not as a fraction of a
   share. The capital basis travels with the data in `rules.sizing_equity`.

The four older strategies (SELL_R1, BREAK_LONG, BREAK_SHORT, and the per-stock
rolling 60/90/197-day win-rate badges) were **switched off in October 2026** after
a 10-year third-party audit found no positive expectancy in them. Per-stock win-rate
badges were also removed: their correlation with the next trade was -0.001. Do not
cite them as current.

## Measured results (out-of-sample 2023-26, net of costs, date-clustered t)
- US: 勝率 60.3%、每單平均淨 1.77%、n = 2,982
- JP: 勝率 65.5%、每單平均淨 2.35%、n = 2,187

Source: 本站自測（Yahoo 10 年日線，同一引擎 A/B，2023–26 樣本外）；含收市企穩 S1 條件。單筆數字，唔等於跑贏被動持有同一批股票，見分析方法論頁

## What these numbers do and do not mean
Read this before citing any figure above.

- **CORRECTION 2026-10-17 — the equal-weight benchmark itself was defective, in
  all three markets.** The old benchmark broadcast each stock's mean daily return
  for the month onto every session of that month, compounding the arithmetic mean
  instead of the realised path. It overstated equal-weight returns by 2.0 to
  3.7pp/yr (US +2.6, Japan +2.0, HK +3.7), i.e. it made the strategy look worse
  than it was. All figures below are recomputed on a true monthly rebalance
  (scripts/hk_retest.py -> data/hk_retest_summary.json). The earlier "27.4% vs
  27.2%, gap is zero" pair quoted from data/portfolio_test.csv is VOID.
- **Per-trade advantage still is not durable excess return.** On the corrected
  benchmark at a uniform 0.25% round-trip cost, US v2 returned 26.0%/yr over
  2016-26 against 24.6%/yr for equal weight (+1.4pp/yr) — but the sign flips
  across sub-windows (+3.7pp in 2016-20, -2.0pp in 2021-26), so it is not a
  stable edge and must not be cited as alpha. The apparent outperformance versus
  a market index is a universe-selection effect, not a timing edge.
- **Japan shows no durable edge either.** At the 0.10% round-trip cost, the same
  comparison gives 18.03%/yr for the v2 portfolio against 15.97%/yr for equal-weight
  holding of the same names over 2016-26 — a gap of +2.06pp/yr, but again unstable
  (-9.1pp/yr in 2016-20, +5.1pp/yr in 2021-26). An earlier +6.9pp/yr
  figure was withdrawn in 2026-09 and must not be cited; almost all of it came from a
  single Nikkei regime (2016-20 TRAILS passive by -7.9pp/yr, only 2021-26 leads, by
  +16.7pp/yr). A point-in-time check that removes the 17
  names which entered the index after 2016-09-01 moves that old gap only +6.9 -> +6.0pp,
  so late entrants are not the cause; but stocks that were large in 2016 and
  later shrank or delisted are absent from every arm and cannot be reconstructed
  from public membership data (our universe is TOPIX Core30+Large70, which overlaps
  the Nikkei 225 change log only 41/201). Do not cite Japan as alpha.
- **The 10-year backtest universe is not point-in-time.** It is today's large caps
  applied retroactively, so every absolute 10-year level carries survivorship bias.
  Only differences between arms running the same stock set are meaningful.
- An earlier site claim of "T+10 +3.02% / +3.05%" was a sum of per-trade
  percentages, not a portfolio return, and has been retracted. Under fixed-capital
  sizing the T+10 portfolio return is -4.05%.

## Data
- T-1 daily OHLC. Hong Kong: Futu OpenD. US and Japan: Yahoo Finance.
- Hong Kong signals are informational only: a short requires borrow availability
  and the cost structure differs.
- Backtests are run on a re-fetched 10-year bar store with a data gate that
  excludes any trade whose window contains a price glitch.
